question.text: Krishna Infra Debt AIF (Cat II) is appointing an independent valuer for the quarterly NAV computation of unlisted portfolio companies. As per the chapter, an independent valuer for AIF must have:

answer.text: A minimum of 3 years of experience in valuation of unlisted securities and be empanelled/qualified in the manner specified by SEBI.
A minimum of 10 years of experience as a merchant banker.
An RBI Category-I Authorised Dealer licence.
A SEBI Research Analyst certification under Regulation 12 of the RA Regulations.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Chapter 7 states: 'Independent valuers should have a minimum of 3 years of experience in valuation of unlisted securities' and compute valuations in the manner specified by SEBI. This is the baseline qualification — APMI empanelment adds operational legitimacy for AIF-specific engagements. **The Trap:** Option B pushes the role to merchant banking. Option C confuses valuer with AD-bank licensing. Option D is a research-analyst cert, unrelated to asset valuation. **Cross-Exam Context:** XXI-B (PM) requires its own valuation framework under PMS Regs; XV (RA) tests recommendation-level analysis. XIX-C managers must also know that under the Companies Act / IBC, an IBBI-registered valuer is required — different from AIF valuer. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Rotate your valuer every 3-5 years just like your statutory auditor. Long-tenure valuers can develop anchor bias toward the Manager's marks — LPs increasingly ask for a valuer independence note in the annual report.
